summary: The page runs as a polished Three.js photographer portfolio. The 3D camera is recognizable and changes through front/lens, side-facing project, reverse-scrolled, and top-down contact views. Project clicks open a readable full-screen article and the floating back action restores the same camera-framed project. Desktop presentation is strong; the 390px layout is usable but omits several lower contact fields, and the transient loader/lens push could not be captured in a delivered screenshot.

runtime.reason: The page loaded with the expected title and rendered a real-time Three.js camera. Camera, project, article, contact, reverse-navigation, mobile, and reload states responded without blocking failures. Console contains one nonblocking favicon 404; page assets returned 200 or 304.

scene.reason: The camera is genuine task-relevant 3D rather than a static image: the lens/front, side-mounted screen and controls, rear projection relationship, and top-down body are visible with coherent perspective, occlusion, materials, and lighting across distinct viewpoints.

checks.reason: Distinct front, project-screen, article-adjacent, and top-down viewpoints expose depth, occlusion, changing scale, and camera geometry. The 390px project view also preserves the screen/body relationship rather than substituting a flat layout.

Typography, monochrome camera materials, muted project palettes, hierarchy, and whitespace form a coherent editorial photography identity. Text remains readable in the intro, project, article, and desktop contact states.

Page-down input advances the scene, project content and backdrop change meaningfully, Enter the Story opens the article, and the floating back action restores the project. These controls provide clear visual state feedback through the primary UI.

Repeat and reverse scrolling worked: Alpine advanced to Amber, PageUp returned to Alpine with the camera framing intact, the article back action returned to the same project, and the home logo returned to the intro. Contact also acted as the tested scroll boundary.

Both 1440x900 and 390x844 layouts were inspected, reload succeeded, lower controls were exercised, and diagnostics were captured. Desktop contact shows email, telephone, studio, and social links. At 390px the contact region contains only email and studio: telephone and Elsewhere are zero-sized, and the page body is overflow hidden, so those lower fields are clipped and unreachable. The only console issue is a favicon 404.

Reloading completed into the intro, and a read-only runtime inspection after load found the loader hidden with the spinner at zero opacity, consistent with the spinner having scaled away. The transient centered white spinner on black was not captured in a delivered screenshot, so its exact appearance and scale-to-zero motion could not be fully verified.

The post-load intro presents a large professional camera head-on with the lens as the visual center and the requested John Doe, Photographer title below. The desktop and narrow views preserve that composition and imply the inside-lens reveal, although intermediate push-out frames were not captured.

Scrolling from the intro changes the view to the camera's rear/screen side, shows the Alpine Silence image and title, and shifts the page backdrop to a matching muted mountain scene. The spatial change from the front lens view is substantial and matches the requested rotation/project presentation.

Advancing from Alpine Silence to Amber Meridian changes the on-screen photograph, title, metadata, and background palette while the camera retains the same project-view position and scale. PageUp reverses cleanly to Alpine Silence.

Scrolling past After Hours reaches a top-down camera view with the photographer contact block below. On desktop, email, telephone, studio address, social links, and back-to-top control are readable; the narrow layout retains the camera and primary email/studio contact content.

Clicking Enter the Story transitions to a full-screen Alpine Silence article with the photograph across the top, a white content field below, black editorial text, and a floating back control. Mouse-wheel scrolling reveals the article body and sidebar metadata.
The floating BACK TO PROJECT action returns to the matching Alpine Silence project, preserving its camera framing, photograph, title, metadata, and Enter the Story control.

instruction.reason: The full narrative and interaction loop is delivered coherently, but the brief's opening spinner/lens-push sequence is only partially verifiable from the captured states; the transient loader and push-out motion were not visually observed.

spatial.reason: Shapes, scale, occlusion, lighting, and materials remain coherent across the front-lens, rear-screen, project, scrolling, and top-down camera viewpoints. The 3D form consistently serves the requested camera-to-project transition.

interaction.reason: Primary sequences, reverse scrolling, article opening, and back recovery are reliable. Local issues remain: PageDown did not scroll the article until the mouse wheel was used, and the mobile chapter controls are small 30x18 targets.

visual.reason: Editorial serif display type, restrained sans-serif labels, monochrome camera materials, and project-specific muted palettes create a purposeful professional-photographer identity. Composition and hierarchy remain legible across the tested major states.

stability.reason: Desktop and mobile flows, reload, and repeated navigation remained usable, and all required assets loaded. The mobile contact view clips telephone and social information because the fixed viewport does not scroll, and there is a harmless favicon 404.

limitations: The black loading screen, centered white spinner, and lens push-out happen before or during page load and were too transient to capture in the delivered screenshot cadence. A post-load DOM probe confirmed #loader was display:none and #spinner opacity:0, but not the full visual sequence.
The exact 180-degree rotation and frame-by-frame smoothness of the camera transitions were inferred from stable before/after states; intermediate animation frames were not recorded.
At 390px, the contact block contains only email and studio. Telephone and Elsewhere elements were present but zero-sized and unreachable because body overflow was hidden.
PageDown advanced the landing/project states but did not move the article body; mouse-wheel scrolling worked. Keyboard focus order was not exhaustively traversed.
No audio content was requested or present, so audio quality was not evaluated.
The 390x844 viewport verifies responsive layout only, not real touch hardware behavior.
Console and network diagnostics are stored in evidence/console.txt and evidence/network.txt; they are discussed here but are not screenshot evidence.
